span: the insurer is not liable for compensation
why: Court states the statutory rule that an unlicensed driver absolves the insurer and then frames the question of the insured's diligence; the outcome is not stated in this passage.

span: The Tribunal absolved the insurer for that reason.
why: Procedural history of an insurer being absolved and directed to pay and recover; the Supreme Court's own holding is elsewhere.

span: the driver was not holding a valid and effective driving licence
why: The insurer's pleading that it is not liable because of the driver's licence; a party submission and not a court finding.

span: the insurer has to indemnify the compensation amount to the third party and the insurance company may recover the same from the insured
why: Headnote holding that the High Court's exoneration of the insurer was set aside and the pay-and-recover award restored; headnote confidence is capped.

span: The Tribunal held that in the absence of a specific authorization to drive a transport vehicle, the liability could not be fastened on the insurer.
why: Tribunal's reasoning and the High Court's inaction; the Supreme Court's view follows in the next paragraph.

span: Mere fact that the driving licence is fake, per se, would not absolve the insurer
why: Headnote holding that a defective licence alone does not absolve the insurer; it is absolved only if the owner knew, which makes the support conditional. Headnote confidence is capped.
